15-Minute Conversation Script (Mentor Check-In)

Participants:
- Mentor: Maya
- Resident: Jordan

[00:00]
Maya: Thanks for making time today, Jordan. Before we jump in, I want to confirm this is our regular weekly check-in and we can talk through work, goals, and anything getting in the way. Does that still work for you?
Jordan: Yeah, that works. I actually wrote a few notes this time because last week I forgot some details when we were wrapping up.
Maya: Perfect. That helps. Start wherever you want. What felt most important this week?
Jordan: The biggest thing is I finished my third week at the warehouse, and I finally feel like I understand the flow. The first week I was lost. Now I can do receiving, scanning, and put-away without asking as many questions.
Maya: That is a big change in a short time. What feedback did you get from your supervisor?
Jordan: He said I am more consistent with timing, and my error count dropped. The first week I had six scanning errors, second week I had three, and this week I had one.
Maya: Nice trend. That gives us something concrete to track.

[01:00]
Maya: Last session you said your goal was to show up on time every shift for two full weeks. How did that go?
Jordan: I was on time for nine out of ten shifts. The one late day was Friday because the bus came twenty minutes late, and then the transfer was delayed too.
Maya: Nine out of ten is still solid. What time does your shift start again?
Jordan: Six-thirty in the morning. I leave at five-fifteen now, but on Fridays the route is weird.
Maya: Do you want to keep the same punctuality goal, or adjust it now that we know Fridays are the risk day?
Jordan: I think adjust it. Maybe a backup transportation plan for Friday mornings, because the other days are pretty stable.
Maya: Good. We can define that as a process goal, not just an outcome goal.
Jordan: Yeah, because being late from transit feels different than oversleeping.

[02:00]
Maya: You also mentioned the forklift certification pathway. Any progress there?
Jordan: Yes. I asked my supervisor, and he said I can enroll in the internal class after ninety days of good attendance. He told me to check back on March 18.
Maya: Great, that gives us a date. What are the prerequisites besides attendance?
Jordan: Safety training modules and one practical assessment. I already completed two of the five online modules. Each one is around thirty minutes.
Maya: So three modules left. Can you realistically finish those this week?
Jordan: I can do two this week and one next week. I do not want to rush because there are quiz questions and you can fail if you click through too fast.
Maya: Sensible. Let’s set two modules by Sunday night, then we review status next session.
Jordan: Works for me.

[03:00]
Maya: How is your energy level with the early schedule? Last month you were sleeping around midnight.
Jordan: That is improving, but still not perfect. I am usually asleep by ten-thirty now. My alarm is at four-forty-five. I get about six hours and fifteen minutes on average.
Maya: Better than before. What is the barrier to getting closer to seven hours?
Jordan: Mostly phone scrolling. I tell myself ten minutes and it turns into forty-five.
Maya: Would a hard cutoff help? Like phone charging outside the bedroom at ten?
Jordan: Probably. I tried it twice this week and fell asleep faster both times.
Maya: Then we should make that specific: phone on kitchen counter by ten p.m. at least five nights this week.
Jordan: I can commit to that.

[04:00]
Maya: Let’s talk money. You said your first full paycheck arrived. What did it look like after taxes?
Jordan: Gross was one thousand forty-eight dollars for two weeks. Net was eight hundred thirty-two.
Maya: And how did you split that?
Jordan: Four hundred for rent contribution, one hundred eighty for groceries, ninety-two for bus pass and rideshare, sixty for phone bill, forty for work boots installment, and I saved sixty.
Maya: That is a clear breakdown. Did anything surprise you?
Jordan: Yeah, food was higher because I bought lunch at work too often. I spent almost seventy just on hot food in the break room.
Maya: Would meal prep reduce that?
Jordan: Definitely. If I pack three lunches a week, I could probably save forty to fifty dollars each pay period.
Maya: That would almost double what you are currently saving.

[05:00]
Maya: On transportation, you mentioned bus delays. How often this month?
Jordan: Four times in three weeks. Two were minor, ten minutes. Two were major, over twenty minutes.
Maya: Did you check if an earlier route exists?
Jordan: There is one at four-fifty, but it means waking up at four. I can do it on Fridays only.
Maya: That sounds like a reasonable backup plan. How much would rideshare cost when transit fails?
Jordan: Around sixteen dollars from my place to work if surge pricing is not crazy. Could be twenty-two on rainy days.
Maya: Do you want to build a small transportation buffer in your budget?
Jordan: Yes, maybe twenty-five dollars per pay period specifically for late-bus emergencies.
Maya: Good. Naming it makes it easier to stick with.

[06:00]
Maya: How is the resume update going?
Jordan: I finished the draft you reviewed. I added my warehouse role, inventory scanner experience, and the volunteer pantry work with numbers.
Maya: Remind me of the pantry numbers you used.
Jordan: I wrote that I helped distribute about one hundred twenty food boxes per week with a team of five volunteers.
Maya: That is strong. Did you apply anywhere new?
Jordan: Two places. One was a shipping coordinator opening, one was a retail stock lead. I got one rejection and one request for a phone screen next Wednesday at two p.m.
Maya: Nice. Which one requested the screen?
Jordan: The shipping coordinator role at Northline Distribution.
Maya: Great. We should prep STAR responses this week.

[07:00]
Maya: Let’s do a quick practice now. Tell me about a time you handled pressure at work.
Jordan: Last Tuesday receiving was overloaded because two trucks came at once. Labels did not match one pallet, and people were waiting on us. I paused, sorted the mismatched items by SKU, checked them against the manifest, and flagged six units that were misrouted.
Maya: Good structure. What was the result?
Jordan: We cleared the dock in forty-five minutes and avoided loading the wrong items into storage. My lead said it prevented rework for the afternoon shift.
Maya: Great example. Add one metric and it is interview-ready.
Jordan: I can say we processed thirty-two pallets before lunch and kept error rate at zero that day.
Maya: Perfect.

[08:00]
Maya: Any workplace issues we should problem-solve?
Jordan: Small one. A coworker keeps changing the scanner settings to large font. Then my scans are slower because the prompt flow changes.
Maya: Have you talked to them directly?
Jordan: Not yet. I did not want it to become a thing.
Maya: You can keep it low drama. Maybe, “Hey, can we leave profile settings on default so handoff is smoother?”
Jordan: Yeah, that sounds normal. I can say it at shift change.
Maya: Good. Assertive and specific, no blame.
Jordan: I need to get better at that. I usually stay quiet, then get annoyed.
Maya: Practicing small boundary conversations helps for bigger ones later.

[09:00]
Maya: How are things at home with your daughter’s school schedule?
Jordan: Better this week. My sister covered pickup Monday and Tuesday. Wednesday I used aftercare. Thursday was rough because aftercare closed early for staff training and I had to leave work ten minutes early.
Maya: Did your supervisor react okay?
Jordan: He was understanding this time, but I do not want that to happen often.
Maya: Can you map all known early-release dates now instead of discovering them same day?
Jordan: Yes, the school posted the calendar. There are three more this semester: March 27, April 24, and May 15.
Maya: Great. Let’s put those in your calendar tonight with reminders one week ahead and one day ahead.
Jordan: I will do that.

[10:00]
Maya: Last month your emergency fund goal was five hundred dollars by June. Where are you now?
Jordan: I was at one hundred forty before this paycheck, then added sixty, so now two hundred.
Maya: You are ahead of pace, actually.
Jordan: Really? I thought I was behind.
Maya: No, because it is still February and you are already forty percent there. If you save sixty per pay period, you reach five hundred in about five more paychecks.
Jordan: That makes me feel better. I think I can push it to seventy-five once lunch spending drops.
Maya: That would shorten the timeline by almost a full pay cycle.
Jordan: Let’s set seventy-five as the target starting next check.

[11:00]
Maya: Are you still interested in the community college logistics certificate for the fall?
Jordan: Yes. I checked tuition. It is one thousand eight hundred for the certificate, but there is a workforce grant that could cover up to seventy percent.
Maya: Did you start the grant application?
Jordan: I created an account but did not upload documents yet. They want proof of income, ID, and a short statement.
Maya: What is the deadline?
Jordan: April 10.
Maya: Then we should break it down. Can you upload income proof and ID by this Saturday, and draft the statement by Tuesday?
Jordan: Yes. The statement is the part I overthink.
Maya: Keep it practical: career goal, timeline, and how training increases pay.

[12:00]
Maya: Let’s capture your near-term goals clearly so there is no ambiguity.
Jordan: Okay.
Maya: Goal one: maintain on-time arrival at least nine of ten shifts, with Friday early-bus backup and rideshare contingency.
Jordan: Yes.
Maya: Goal two: complete two forklift safety modules by Sunday and the final module next week.
Jordan: Yes.
Maya: Goal three: phone outside bedroom by ten p.m. at least five nights.
Jordan: Yes.
Maya: Goal four: pack lunch at least three shifts per week to reduce food spending by forty dollars per pay period.
Jordan: Yes.
Maya: Goal five: save seventy-five from next paycheck toward emergency fund.
Jordan: Yes, and keep it in the separate savings account, not checking.
Maya: Good addition.

[13:00]
Maya: Any blockers that could prevent those goals?
Jordan: Fatigue is still the biggest one, then transportation on Fridays, and sometimes last-minute school notices.
Maya: For fatigue, we already have the phone cutoff. For transportation, we have early Friday bus plus emergency rideshare budget. For school notices, we are pre-loading calendar dates. Anything else?
Jordan: Maybe motivation dips after a hard shift. I come home and do nothing productive.
Maya: Then let’s create a minimum viable routine for hard days: ten-minute reset, quick meal, then one small task only.
Jordan: I like that better than forcing a big to-do list.
Maya: Exactly. The point is consistency.
Jordan: I can make the one small task either module progress or grant application progress.

[14:00]
Maya: Before we close, I want you to summarize your commitments in your own words.
Jordan: Sure. I will use the earlier bus on Fridays and keep twenty-five dollars per paycheck for emergency rides. I will finish two forklift modules by Sunday, one next week. I will charge my phone in the kitchen by ten p.m. at least five nights. I will pack lunch at least three days each week and move seventy-five dollars from my next check into savings.
Maya: Great summary. What support do you need from me before next session?
Jordan: Can you send me three interview questions to practice for the Northline phone screen, and maybe review my grant statement draft?
Maya: Yes. I will send questions tonight and give feedback on your draft within twenty-four hours after you share it.
Jordan: Perfect. I feel a lot more organized than last week.
Maya: You did strong work this week. We will meet again next Thursday at seven p.m. and review the same metrics plus interview outcome.
Jordan: Sounds good. Thanks, Maya.
Maya: See you next week.

[Post-Conversation Notes Embedded in Script]
Jordan: Wait, one last thing I forgot. My supervisor offered one optional Saturday shift next weekend, four hours at time-and-a-half. Should I take it?
Maya: If childcare is covered and rest is still protected, yes, one extra shift could help your emergency fund. Just avoid stacking too many overtime shifts while your sleep routine is stabilizing.
Jordan: Childcare is covered that Saturday. If I take it, net pay might add around sixty to seventy dollars.
Maya: Then take this one and earmark at least fifty of that extra pay directly to savings.
Jordan: Done. I’ll treat it as a one-time boost, not a new baseline.
Maya: Good framing. Also, confirm your phone screen details: date, time, and quiet location.
Jordan: Wednesday, March 4, at 2:00 p.m. I can do it from the library study room.
Maya: Reserve the room now if possible. Arrive fifteen minutes early with your notes and water.
Jordan: I’ll reserve it right after this call.
Maya: Excellent. Now we are really done.
